transcript.text: Alright, I've heard from everyone and I think I have enough to make my decision. Let me lay it out. First, donation is off the table — Rosa, you've made clear that Uncle wanted this boat kept in the family and used for the annual river cleanup, and I'm honoring that. Second, we're keeping the boat and using it for the river-cleanup morning on June 6, 2027 at 08:00 — Eli, you committed to that date, and it lines up with Uncle's wishes, so we're going to meet it. But I want to be clear: that kind of commitment does not happen again without coming to me first. Third, for storage, we're taking Martin up on his offer — covered garage through October 31, 2027, with the boat on a wall-mounted cradle. Priya, thank you for bringing that forward. Fourth, for restoration: we'll do the stripping and epoxy sealing here at my house while the boat is still on the sawhorses, where we know we have space and can manage ventilation. Once the epoxy has cured for the full seven days, we'll mount it on the cradle and move it to Martin's garage. Working backward from June 6, the epoxy needs to be fully cured by June 5 at the latest, which means the sealing needs to be done by May 29. Stripping has to be complete before that, so I want the stripping work to begin no later than May 22 — that gives us a week for stripping and sealing, then seven full days of cure. Eli and Rosa, you both offered to help — I'm taking you up on that. Eli, you're on cradle-building duty since you created the time pressure. Rosa, I'd like your help with the stripping and prep work. Jonah, you're our point person on the epoxy process since you've already talked to the surveyor — make sure we're following the steps correctly. Priya, go ahead and confirm with Martin that the garage space is still available and get any details we need for the cradle installation. Once the boat is cured and on the cradle, we'll move it to Martin's garage for storage, and it'll be ready to transport to the river by June 6. That's my decision.
